clue.text: Do business-if craft is used

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are used up and put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A trader wonders whether a boat will help with the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To traffic is to trade or deal in goods, often illicitly.

clue.text: Beam as son breaks into a vehicle

indicators.note: into places the scrambled word inside the vehicle

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails

indicators.note: breaks means the word son is broken and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy smashes his way into a tram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' turns SON into NSO, which 'into' puts inside TRAM; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar over a door or window.

clue.text: Seeks poisoners with outrage!

indicators.note: with here means the snakes hold the anger among them

parts.note: asps are venomous snakes, poisoners
ire is anger or outrage

explanation.surface: Someone hunts murderers who used poison, in fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poisoners' suggests killers, but it means snakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to aim for or strive after something.

clue.text: Assume American soldier will be caught up in a boggy area

indicators.note: caught means held inside the marsh

parts.note: a fen is a marsh

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the soldier is read from bottom to top

parts.note: GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A GI expects to be trapped in a swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GI into IG, which 'caught' puts inside FEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign is to put on or pretend, as one assumes an air.

clue.text: Stock enclosure

parts.note: stock means livestock, such as cows
a pen is a fenced enclosure

explanation.definitionFit: A fenced place where livestock are kept is a pen for cows.

clue.text: Rules to be observed about a German analgesic

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second, wrapping it

parts.note: a code is a set of rules to be followed
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A list of regulations concerning a German painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts EIN inside CODE, splitting it COD...E.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is an opiate drug used to relieve pain.

clue.text: Net doesn't obstruct the view

explanation.surface: A mesh that leaves the outlook open.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear profit is what remains after deductions, as net does; clear glass or air lets you see through it.

clue.text: Mad artist mistaken for a writer

indicators.note: mistaken says the two words are set out wrongly, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A crazy painter is confused with an author.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatist is a writer of plays.

clue.text: Showing spirit, see about appeal

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous sprite or spirit
lo is an old word meaning look or see
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: With spirit, someone looks into a plea.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to beg or plead earnestly.

clue.text: The section empowered to provide heating

explanation.surface: A part that is authorised to keep things warm.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the electric heating part in a kettle or heater, 'empowered' hinting at electric power.
explanation.definitionFit: An element is a component part; it is also the wire coil that heats in an electric appliance.

clue.text: Pop back, meaning to settle

indicators.note: back says this short word for father is read from right to left

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father, as is pa
the point of something is its meaning

explanation.surface: A father returns, intending to sort things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PA into AP.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint a time or place is to fix or settle it.

clue.text: Standard lamp smashed and dumped in the river

indicators.note: something dumped in the river goes inside its name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a favourite crossword river

indicators.note: smashed means the word lamp is broken up and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a standard lamp and throws it into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' turns LAMP into AMPL, which 'dumped in' places inside EXE.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a model to be copied, as an example is.

clue.text: A killer, one not known to accept money

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the money goes inside

parts.note: a stranger is a person one does not know
L stands for pounds, as in the old symbol for sterling

explanation.surface: A murderer who is an unknown person agrees to take a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes into STRANGER between G and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler is a murderer who kills by throttling.

clue.text: Pole composing poetry

explanation.surface: A Polish writer busy with verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a Polish person but is an electrode; the second reading splits the answer into two words, a lyric poem being composed.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a pole of a battery; one writing a lyric poem is at work on a verse piece, the second sense.

clue.text: Make a request in writing for hides

indicators.note: in places the request inside the abbreviation for writing

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
to ask is to make a request

explanation.surface: Someone puts in a written application for animal skins.
explanation.definitionFit: Masks cover and conceal the face, so they are things that conceal.

clue.text: Rush-flourishing plant

parts.note: to speed is to rush
well means healthy or thriving

explanation.surface: A bulrush thriving in a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' suggests a waterside plant, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a small blue-flowered wild plant, veronica.

clue.text: Manager shedding quiet tear about team

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

indicators.note: about means the tear goes round the team

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A football manager sheds a quiet tear over the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shedding' joins the pieces in the surface; 'about' puts SIDE inside RENT, then P goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head who directs an organisation or company.

clue.text: Really delightful, so absorbing the listener in the finish

indicators.note: absorbing means the finish takes the listener inside itself

parts.note: an ending is a finish
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A truly charming conclusion that grips the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Endearing means charming, inspiring affection.

clue.text: Being no longer in credit, Edward is worried

indicators.note: in places the phrase meaning formerly inside the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the abbreviation for credit in accounts
once means formerly, no longer so
Ned is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward is anxious because his bank account is overdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a link: ONCE goes inside CR, then NED follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerned means anxious or troubled about something.

clue.text: Charles the Tenth's discipline

parts.note: the tenth in a line of kings is numbered ten

explanation.surface: A French king's way of keeping order.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles X was a king of France; the regnal number ten follows the short name.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to correct or subdue by punishment.

clue.text: Hurried up over class report

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ran means hurried
a rate is a class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: Someone rushes over to give a top-class account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAN into NAR; 'over' places it above RATE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell or recount a story.

clue.text: A little extra item that's characteristic

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small added bonus that is typical of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a distinguishing feature or quality.

clue.text: Fishy affairs could well be brought to public notice

definitions.text: Fishy affairs could well be brought to public notice

parts.words: Fishy affairs could well be brought to public notice
parts.note: the fishy things are not scandals but tanks of fish put on display for visitors

explanation.surface: Shady dealings are likely to be exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishy affairs' suggests scandal; they are literal glass tanks of fish shown to the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria are tanks or buildings displaying living fish.

clue.text: A lever altered as required

indicators.note: as required means the letters are put into whatever order is needed

explanation.surface: A mechanism changed to suit the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' looks like the anagram signal for the lever, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a foot-operated lever, as on a sewing machine.

clue.text: There's a large number to deliver, sharp!

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
to rid is to deliver or free from

explanation.surface: A postman barks about the many parcels still to drop off.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means pungent or biting, as a smell or remark can be.

clue.text: Giving coppers freedom of action appears commonplace

parts.note: coppers are pennies, abbreviated p
latitude is scope or freedom to act

explanation.surface: Letting police officers do as they please seems routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but it is copper coins, pennies.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a trite remark, a commonplace used as a noun.

clue.text: Flatten reporters!

explanation.surface: An order to crush the journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: To press is to squash flat; the press is the body of journalists.

clue.text: The matter is to go to court

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action in court

explanation.surface: The point in dispute is to be taken to law.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a topic or point in question.

clue.text: An athletic person finds this highly dependable

definitions.text: An athletic person finds this highly dependable

parts.words: An athletic person finds this highly dependable
parts.note: an acrobat relies on this swinging bar high above the circus ring, literally depending from it

explanation.surface: A sportsman praises some reliable equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highly dependable' means hanging up high, the way a circus bar is suspended.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a bar hung high on ropes for acrobats to swing from.

clue.text: Crumbling ruins a newspaperman covered

indicators.note: crumbling means the word ruins falls apart and is rebuilt in another order

parts.note: ed is short for editor, a newspaperman

explanation.surface: A journalist reports on decaying ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbling' turns RUINS into INSUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Insured means protected by a policy against loss.

clue.text: Losing one second is undesirable and causes irritation

indicators.note: losing signals that one letter is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: something needless is unwanted, so undesirable
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Wasting even a second is annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing' removes one S from NEEDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke or annoy them.

clue.text: Angered-devastated-by an explosive device

indicators.note: devastated says the letters of the angry word are wrecked and reformed

explanation.surface: An enraged person is shattered by a bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small bomb thrown by hand.
